newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian wheat imports seen dampening prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian wheat imports seen dampening prices.

text.p: India's decision to import two milion tonnes of wheat has affected domestic prices marginally but a further drop is expected when shipments start arriving in January, analysts and traders said on Friday.
India late on Thursday said it would purchase two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March) to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices.
On Friday, the government allowed flour mills to freely import wheat to meet their requirements for milling and for the sale of flour in the domestic market.
Traders said wheat prices fell 1,500 rupees per tonne on an average in Delhi markets and by 1,000 rupees per tonne in Bombay markets on news of government imports.
They said wheat prices had started showing a downward trend since Monday on reports that India would make substantial imports to augment stocks.
"By the time the imported wheat starts coming in January it will definitely bring down the prices and bring out hoarded stocks," said Mulraj Tanna, a leading Bombay foodgrain trader.
"The very announcement of imports brought down prices. Once the first vessel arrives, prices will have a further setback," said one analyst.

Dwindling government reserves have caused domestic wheat prices to rise sharply in recent months compared to prices last year. Traders said there was a 40 percent increase in wheat prices in the last six months.
Wheat stocks fell mainly due to a drop in procurement by the state-owned Food Corporation of India (FCI).
Government wheat procurement in the 1995/96 growing season fell to 8.2 million tonnes from 12.3 million the previous year due to a three-million tonne shortfall in output.
As of October 1, FCI held 19.6 million tonnes of foodgrains -- wheat, rice and other cereals -- against 29.9 million tonnes a year earlier.
A senior official of India's state-run State Trading Corporation confirmed on Friday that it had bought one million tonnes of wheat from Australia for delivery starting in January.
The official said it was also looking at sellers in Argentina, Canada and the European Union for purchase of the other one million allowed by the government.

The last time India imported two million tonnes of wheat was in 1991/92 (April/March). It exported 600,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.07 million tonnes up to September 30 this year, when the government halted further exports.
